label: The Dvapara Yuga
summary: Third of the four ages. Tradition gives it 864,000 years with twilights, and dharma on two legs. The Mahabharata tradition places its great war at the end of this age.

label: Dharma on two legs
summary: In Dvapara, the bull of dharma stands on two legs, compassion and truthfulness, according to the Bhagavata Purana.

label: Krishna, the eighth avatar
summary: Krishna is the avatar linked to the Dvapara age in the common list. Some lists put Balarama in the eighth place and Krishna ninth, so the list varies by tradition.

label: The Vedas divided in four
summary: Tradition says the single Veda was divided into Rig, Sama, Yajur and Atharva in this age. Vyasa, to whom the Mahabharata is also credited, is the traditional divider.

summary: Most scholars date the bulk of the Mahabharata text between about the 3rd century BCE and 3rd century CE, with the oldest parts no earlier than about 400 BCE.
